tytul: Whole or halved tomatoes packed in tomato juice (NCHFP)
wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for whole or halved tomatoes packed in tomato juice, with added acid, processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:ACI-053]

akapity: According to an FDA list, tomatoes have an approximate pH of 4.30–4.90, and the value varies widely with variety and conditions. [T:ACI-093]
Sugar may be added to balance the acidic taste, but the acid must not be left out. [T:ACI-047]
Wash the tomatoes, dip them in boiling water for 30–60 seconds or until the skins split, then dip them in cold water. [T:ACI-196]
Slip off the skins, remove the cores and leave the tomatoes whole or cut them in half. [T:ACI-196]
Add the bottled lemon juice or citric acid to the jars, and if you like, 1 teaspoon of salt per quart jar. [T:ACI-196]
Add 2 tablespoons of bottled lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid per quart jar (about 0.95 l) of tomatoes. [T:ACI-044]
For pint jars, use 1 tablespoon of bottled lemon juice or 1/4 teaspoon of citric acid. [T:ACI-045]

JarAtlas rule for metric jars: to a jar larger than a pint, of up to 946 ml (for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l), add acid as for a quart: 2 tablespoons of bottled lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid. [T:ACI-193]
Raw pack: heat tomato juice in a saucepan and fill the jars with raw tomatoes, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-197]
Cover the tomatoes in the jars with hot tomato juice, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-197]
Hot pack: put the tomatoes in a large saucepan, add enough tomato juice to cover them completely and boil gently for 5 minutes. [T:ACI-198]
Fill the jars with hot tomatoes, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace, and add hot tomato juice to cover them, again leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm). [T:ACI-198]
For both packs, put on the lids and process. [T:ACI-198]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m), for hot or raw pack, process pint and quart jars in a boiling-water bath for 85 minutes. [T:ACI-053,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints and quarts for 90 minutes. [T:ACI-199,ACI-176]
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints and quarts for 95 minutes. [T:ACI-200,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints and quarts for 100 minutes. [T:ACI-201,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml. [T:ACI-174]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): this recipe has the same time for pints and quarts, so a jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, gets that time. [T:ACI-175]
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so JarAtlas recommends smaller jars. [T:ACI-175]
